# Six EAFIT graduates among the 20 most innovative leaders in Colombia

**Carlos Ignacio Gallego, president of Grupo Nutresa; Diego Loaiza, general manager for the Andean and Caribbean region of Grupo Familia; David Escobar Arango, director of Comfama; Claudia Restrepo Montoya, rector of EAFIT; Santiago Londoño, general manager of Haceb, and Luis Alberto Botero, president of Alianza Team.**

**These six graduates from different EAFIT programs have something in common: Forbes magazine included them in its list of the 20 most innovative leaders in the country for being agents of change who foster innovation, generate a positive impact in their sectors, and contribute to economic and social development.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- [Our Impact](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias/nuestro-impacto)
- Six EAFIT Graduates Among Colombia's 20 Most Innovative Leaders

![Image: Six EAFIT graduates among the 20 most innovative leaders in Colombia](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/92df2b48-b469-4c1d-88a8-200da086c992/web/graduados-eafitenses-forbes.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=g1NBEjj_)

Forbes' criteria for this list include media reputation for innovation, value creation, and strategic initiatives for the coming year. Among the EAFIT alumni recognized are two engineers, two administrators, one with a master's degree in administration, and one finance specialist.

Carlos Ignacio Gallego Palacio, president of Grupo Nutresa; Diego Loaiza, general manager for the Andean and Caribbean region of Grupo Familia; David Escobar Arango, director of Comfama; Claudia Restrepo Montoya, rector of EAFIT; Santiago Londoño Aguilar, general manager of Haceb, and Luis Alberto Botero, President of Alianza Team; all graduates of EAFIT, have been recognized among the 20 most innovative leaders in Colombia, according to _Forbes_ .

The list recognizes its members as agents of change who foster innovation, generate a positive impact in their sectors, and contribute to economic and social development. Furthermore, it acknowledges their role in redefining how business is done, according to the publication, “from adopting cutting-edge technologies to implementing sustainable strategies and creating disruptive business models.” Academics from business schools and specialized consultants participated in its creation, analyzing innovation indicators.

Isabel Gómez Yepes, Director of Institutional Development and Outreach, the department within the University that leads the connection between the university and its graduates, states that this news “is a source of pride because these are leaders who are contributing to society from the different sectors in which they work. They are leaders with very interesting business trajectories, with impact and influence, and who are generating a true transformation in society.”

Two of the six leaders recognized by Forbes are graduates of the School of Applied Sciences and Engineering: Carlos Ignacio Gallego, president of Grupo Nutresa, is a civil engineer, while David Escobar Arango, director of Comfama, is a production engineer. According to Ricardo Taborda Ríos, dean of the School, “Although they graduated a few decades ago, they are characterized by their holistic approach to problems, and that is a fact we must highlight, because EAFIT not only graduates excellent professionals, but also individuals who transcend their disciplines and exercise comprehensive leadership. In other words, they are very good engineers, but they are also very good administrators, leaders, managers, creators, and motivators of change and reform. I believe these two exemplify this perfectly.”

Graduates of the School of Management include leaders Claudia Restrepo Montoya, rector of EAFIT, and Luis Alberto Botero, president of Alianza Team; Santiago Londoño, manager of Haceb, also earned a master's degree in Administration and completed a specialization in Marketing; and finally, Diego Loaiza, from Grupo Familia, completed a specialization in Finance.

According to Cristina Vélez Valencia, Dean of the School of Administration, “this is a demonstration that EAFIT is a university connected with organizations from its beginnings, and that its interest in training the leaders of companies, of the business ecosystem of the region, of Colombia, of Antioquia, has materialized in exceptional leaderships such as those of the people we see highlighted.”

These recognitions add to other positions of EAFI graduates in rankings such as the 11 who lead seven of the 100 start-ups recognized by Forbes in 2024 or the 16 who are part of the Mercolíderes list, which speaks to the commitment of the graduates to impact and have a positive influence on society, from different roles.

###### Viruses versus bacteria: PhageLife's proposal for the swine sector from EAFIT

On a pig farm, a bacterial infection can jeopardize the animals' health and the farm's productivity. Furthermore, the problem becomes more complex when the bacteria stop responding to the antibiotics that previously combated them. To explore another approach, the company [PhageLife](https://phagelife.co/) is developing customized solutions using bacteriophages, naturally occurring viruses capable of eliminating specific bacteria.
